manuscript_sentence: The avian eggshell is a load-bearing mineralized organ whose mechanical performance is established at the level of the mammillary layer, where calcite growth is initiated on organic-matrix nucleation centers. Although the shell also regulates gas exchange, microbial defense, and embryonic calcium supply, its resistance to fracture depends disproportionately on how densely mammillae are packed and how effectively mineral is organized around them. The mammillary layer is therefore not simply the innermost shell compartment; it is the structural origin of whole-shell mechanics.

supporting_sentence: Background The avian eggshell is a natural protective envelope that relies on the phenomenon of biomineralization for its formation.

manuscript_sentence: Work over the past two decades has identified uterine matrix proteins as major regulators of mammillary nucleation, crystal growth orientation, and shell architecture, with ovalbumin (OVAL) and ovocleidin-116 (OC116) among the best-supported Ca²⁺-responsive factors. These proteins carry N-linked glycans that vary from compact High-Mannose to extended Sialylated Complex forms, and prior structural work has shown that glycan occupancy can alter conformation and the solvent exposure of acidic residues involved in Ca²⁺ coordination. In parallel, comparative morphometry and simulation studies have shown that eggshell mechanics diverge systematically across the precocial–altricial spectrum. What remains missing is a single cross-species framework connecting these observations. Specifically, it is not known whether species-level divergence in OVAL glycan class is translated into predictable differences in Ca²⁺ accessibility, mammillary packing, and shell mechanical performance.

manuscript_sentence: Here, we test that cross-scale mechanism by integrating micro-CT morphometry, comparative eggshell matrix proteomics with gene-family evolution analysis, intact glycopeptide mass spectrometry, Re-Glyco structural ensemble modelling, and finite-element simulation in three species — Gallus gallus, Anas platyrhynchos, and Columba livia — representing, respectively, the precocial terrestrial ground-nesting, precocial semi-aquatic, and altricial elevated-nesting ecological guilds. By traversing from whole-shell morphology through proteome-wide orthogroup comparison and atomic-level electrostatic modeling to tissue-scale contact-stress simulation, we show that species-specific N-glycan class composition on OVAL tracks a gradient in Ca²⁺ accessibility, mammillary density, and shear resistance. manuscript_sentence: Calcium ecology adds a second layer of constraint. Terrestrial species rely largely on diet, medullary bone mobilization, and incidental mineral supplementation from substrate, whereas aquatic and semi-aquatic species can access calcium-rich prey more continuously during shell formation. This means that species can differ not only in how much shell protection they require, but also in how calcium is provisioned during the narrow window of uterine mineralization. A mechanistic explanation for eggshell diversity must therefore accommodate both developmental strategy and calcium availability.

manuscript_sentence: Gene-family evolution was strongly asymmetric across the three lineages, despite recovery of the expected Galloanserae phylogeny. G. gallus and A. platyrhynchos formed the sister pair and C. livia the outgroup. Within that framework, CAFE5 revealed that chicken showed net contraction, duck was intermediate, and pigeon showed net expansion (Fig. 4a,b). The contracted chicken families were enriched for immune functions, whereas expanded pigeon families were enriched for transmembrane transport, Rho signaling, and synapse-associated processes. These genomic trends establish that the three shell-forming systems are evolutionarily distinct, but they also frame an important point for the present study: lineage divergence is broad, whereas the shell phenotype we seek to explain is sharply ordered.

manuscript_sentence: Across birds, reproductive strategy and nesting ecology impose different constraints on how much mineralized protection the egg must provide. Precocial lineages generally produce shells that tolerate greater environmental and hatch-related mechanical demands, whereas altricial lineages often operate under reduced structural requirements associated with elevated or otherwise protected nests. These life-history differences imply that mammillary architecture should be an adaptive trait, but they do not by themselves explain what molecular mechanism tunes one shell system toward dense nucleation and another toward a more weakly mineralized state.

manuscript_sentence: Work over the past two decades has identified uterine matrix proteins as major regulators of mammillary nucleation, crystal growth orientation, and shell architecture, with ovalbumin (OVAL) and ovocleidin-116 (OC116) among the best-supported Ca²⁺-responsive factors. These proteins carry N-linked glycans that vary from compact High-Mannose to extended Sialylated Complex forms, and prior structural work has shown that glycan occupancy can alter conformation and the solvent exposure of acidic residues involved in Ca²⁺ coordination. In parallel, comparative morphometry and simulation studies have shown that eggshell mechanics diverge systematically across the precocial–altricial spectrum. What remains missing is a single cross-species framework connecting these observations. Specifically, it is not known whether species-level divergence in OVAL glycan class is translated into predictable differences in Ca²⁺ accessibility, mammillary packing, and shell mechanical performance.

manuscript_sentence: OVAL ortholog protein structures (AlphaFold2-predicted models) were accessed through the GlycoShape platform (glycoshape.org) via UniProt accession identifiers. Experimentally detected N-glycan compositions from IGP-MS were mapped to the GlycoShape glycan library by monoisotopic mass matching (tolerance ±0.5 Da), using per-residue masses of 203.0794 Da (HexNAc), 162.0528 Da (Hex), 291.0954 Da (NeuAc), 146.0579 Da (dHex), and 132.0423 Da (Pen) with an 18.0106 Da water correction; matched entries were retrieved as GlyTouCan accession identifiers. Full conformational ensembles were then generated with the GlycoShape Re-Glyco Ensemble tool (glycoshape.org/ensemble), which restores missing glycans by aligning them to torsion angles from Privateer crystallographic standards and sampling conformations from the GlycoShape molecular-dynamics ensemble library. For each protein, a session was created via the GlycoShape API to identify available N-glycosylation sequons in the structural model; each matched glycan was then submitted as an independent modelling job and attached to the target sequon — G. gallus N293 and A. platyrhynchos / C. livia N97 — with ensemble size 50, random seed 42, and PDB output format. This procedure yielded 50 glycoprotein models for G. gallus (1 matched glycan type), 150 for A. platyrhynchos (3 types), and 700 for C. livia (14 types, including four NeuAc positional isomers resolved from the GlycoShape library). Ensemble geometric descriptors were calculated for each model from atomic coordinates using BioPython: the radius of gyration (Rg) of all glycan heavy atoms, the end-to-end distance of the glycan chain, and the minimum distance between any glycan heavy atom and protein Cα atoms (minimum Cα contact distance). Per-structure summary statistics (mean ± s.d.) and pairwise species comparisons (Mann–Whitney U test, two-tailed) were performed for each descriptor.
